Key Finding: Brooklyn and Manhattan carry the highest average scores (~20.7). Unknown/unassigned borough records skew highest at 22.5 — a data quality gap in high-turnover areas.
Key Finding: Bangladeshi (30.8) and African (28.2) cuisines lead on average scores. Risk is structural — inherent to complex raw-food preparation — not just individual behavior. This supports sector-specific education over penalties.
Key Finding: Pest Control and Temperature violations dominate — these are the highest-leverage intervention points for regulators.
Key Finding: Random Forest achieves 80% accuracy and the best F1 score (0.47). Cuisine type contributed ~80% of feature importance — confirming structural risk over individual behavior.

6.4× lift: Prioritizing High-tier restaurants means inspectors find actual violations 6.4× more often than random scheduling.
How to use: Each dot is one restaurant. Red = High Risk, Orange = Medium, Green = Low Risk. Click legend items to show/hide risk groups. Hover over any dot to see the restaurant name, borough, and score. Zoom and pan to explore neighborhoods.
